newsitem.title: USA: New Orleans port delays seen lifting freight rates.
newsitem.headline: New Orleans port delays seen lifting freight rates.

text.p: Grain freight rates could get a boost following a ship accident in New Orleans over the weekend, which curtailed freighter traffic at one of the world's biggest ports and backed up vessels in the Mississippi River, shipbrokers said.
While the North Atlantic market was typically quiet at the start of the week, brokers said the impact on rates would increase as the delays at the port persisted.
"It will be somewhat supportive in the short-term because of the congestion," said one broker. "There is no way for anything but a small ship get through that blockage."
"If you're in a berth you can't vacate because there is no place to go."
The Cosco-owned bulk freighter, the Bright Field, slammed into a waterfront shopping complex in New Orleans on Saturday as it navigated down-river.
By late Monday, the Coast Guard had yet to determine when or how the Bright Field would be moved. All traffic at the port was likely to be affected until at least the end of the week, officials said.

Cargo movement in the vicinity of the accident was limited to smaller ships, though the Coast Guard eased the restrictions somewhat Monday afternoon to allow ships of up to 25-foot drafts to proceed down-river. Inbound traffic was restricted to 30-foot drafts.
Under normal conditions, the maximum draft at New Orleans is 45 feet.
All but one of the main grain elevators at the port were located north of where the accident occurred, while the port's major coals terminals are well down-river, shippers said.
With so much uncertainty surrounding the salvage efforts, brokers said many operators may have decided to hold off on doing business at higher rates.
"Most of December has fixed already, so I imagine people are going to wait and see what happens," another broker said. ((-- Wendy Pollack, New York Commodities Desk +1 212 859 1640))
